text_blocks.speaker: Tracy McGrady
text_blocks.text: Before Brunson signed with the Philadelphia 76ers, I looked at them as a contender with Jaylen Brown. We had the conversation with Anfernee Simons. That signing, I felt like, all right, having these two pieces along with Maxey, VJ, and Joel Embiid, if healthy, man, I see them being a team that's going to be something to reckon with to be able to come out of the East.

quotes.speaker: Tracy McGrady
quotes.summary_phrase: Tracy McGrady on the impact of adding Jalen Brunson to the 76ers
quotes.excerpt: Now you have somebody that you can rely on in these precious situations that you trust to have
quotes.quote: Now you have somebody that you can rely on in these precious situations that you trust to have the ball in his hands. Basketball decisions are going to be made. The right basketball decisions are going to be made. And now you can utilize Maxey's speed, VJ's athleticism. Jalen Brunson is one of the best back-door cutting players there is. He's going to get a lot of those from Brunson because the pass and him being able to see over the defense. I like that in terms of taking loads off of young players having to be out in front so early to lead this team to a championship.

quotes.speaker: Vince Carter
quotes.summary_phrase: Vince Carter on Tyrese Maxey's growth and readiness for the moment
quotes.excerpt: I do think Tyrese Maxey is ready for the moment prior to Brunson coming. I do.
quotes.quote: I do think Tyrese Maxey is ready for the moment prior to Brunson coming. I do. I mean, I know you said the experience of the championship, so that's different. But I just felt like he, once he got the keys to that organization, he became a different player in my opinion. You got to understand, he didn't know how to play with Joel Embiid. He was struggling with that in the beginning. And then once he realized it was his team, he became a different player. I felt like he was on another level.

quotes.speaker: Tracy McGrady
quotes.summary_phrase: Tracy McGrady on Joel Embiid being the X-factor for the 76ers
quotes.excerpt: We know who they are. They're going to be vital parts to this. We know who they are. We don't know
quotes.quote: We know who they are. They're going to be vital parts to this. We know who they are. We don't know what we're getting for Joel Embiid. We don't know. We know if he's healthy, we know what we get from him if he's healthy. But we don't know how many times we're going to have him available. So he's the X-factor.

quotes.speaker: Vince Carter
quotes.summary_phrase: Vince Carter on the importance of the 76ers' backup center
quotes.excerpt: I feel like a X-factor is your backup center has to be whoever that may be because of what you're saying
quotes.quote: I feel like a X-factor is your backup center has to be whoever that may be because of what you're saying. If for some reason Joel Embiid is not available, yes, I know you can play Brunson at the five. I get it. I get it. But I still think Adem Bona is going to have to have a big year. If Joel Embiid is not healthy, it ain't working.

quotes.summary_phrase: Anfernee Simons on the origin of his name
quotes.excerpt: My dad was big, big Penny fan. So, you know, he obviously around the game of basketball played it
quotes.quote: My dad was big, big Penny fan. So, you know, he obviously around the game of basketball played it, you know, obviously in the program and stuff. So, my parents just named me Anfernee. Um, they thought it was unique name and obviously, you know, I was kind of destined to play basketball. So, that's where the name came from.

quotes.speaker: Tracy McGrady
quotes.summary_phrase: Tracy McGrady on the impact of Penny Hardaway in Central Florida

quotes.quote: Being from that area and when we drafted Penny, and Penny put on that pinstripe uniform, bro, if you were from Orlando, if you were from that Central Florida area, you had no other choice but to fall in love with Penny. Because he was that nice. Like he had that type of flair in game to where you identify yourself like, yo, he cold, bro. And he had that type of an effect on real like people that love the game of basketball.

quotes.speaker: Anfernee Simons
quotes.summary_phrase: Anfernee Simons on why he chose to play for Philadelphia
quotes.excerpt: For me, I think it's his, you know, playing on that big stage. I think, you know, I had opportunity
quotes.quote: For me, I think it's his, you know, playing on that big stage. I think, you know, I had opportunity to do that obviously in, in, in Boston. And then, um, you know, obviously the trade happened. So, um, I wasn't able to, you know, able to be in the playoffs that season. I was super excited for that season. But, um, you know, I just needed to go somewhere for sure that was going to be a good fit for me and I was going to be able to go in the playoffs and show what I can really do.

quotes.speaker: Anfernee Simons
quotes.summary_phrase: Anfernee Simons on the mentors who helped him early in his career
quotes.excerpt: There was a lot of guys that that helped me along the way whether it was, you know, Norman Powell
quotes.quote: There was a lot of guys that that helped me along the way whether it was, you know, Norman Powell helped me out a lot. You know, CJ McCollum helped me out a lot. You know, just from those guys that didn't necessarily come into the league starting. You know, um, you know, obviously Damian Lillard came into the league and immediately he was a starter and he became all-star pretty quickly. But for guys like that, they had to work their way up. And so at an early age, I kind of gravitated to them as well because I was in the same position.

quotes.quote: They always felt like, you know, you go you a starter, but for right now, until you become that, you need to learn how to be able to play a role and, you know, do it well.

quotes.quote: I want to be able to be professional. You know what I mean? I want to walk through the door, walk through any any door in any organization and be like the last organization can say, man, he handled himself well. He's a he's a pros pro. And that just spreads around the league.

quotes.speaker: Anfernee Simons
quotes.summary_phrase: Anfernee Simons on the mental challenge of being traded
quotes.excerpt: That can easily break a player. You know what I'm saying? And how they handle the rest of that season,
quotes.quote: That can easily break a player. You know what I'm saying? And how they handle the rest of that season, it, you know, everybody is watching it, which I think young guys don't realize that all the time. It's like, okay, it didn't work out, you moved on here, but how do you handle it now? Because somebody else is watching because, yeah, that deal is up, you're going to be out there giving your agent going to be out there calling people like trying to get you on another team, and they're going to revert back to how you handle your situation.

quotes.speaker: Anfernee Simons

Um, obviously JT ended up coming back. Um, and so that's what they they feel the need that they feel like they needed. It made sense.

text_blocks.speaker: Vince Carter
text_blocks.text: If you had to pick a team, and you could join LeBron James and Jaylen Brown in Philadelphia, would you do it?

text_blocks.speaker: Anfernee Simons
text_blocks.text: It would be crazy. Obviously, playing with guys like that, it makes the game so much easier. You don't have to do as much. You can just play your role, play your game, and let them do what they do. It would be a fun experience.

text_blocks.speaker: Tracy McGrady
text_blocks.text: That's a championship-level squad right there.
